 Search How to File a Tax Refund Claim in the Philippines: BIR Rules, Documents and Denials
 Atty. Yasser R. Aureada, CPA Sep 10 11 min read Updated: 6 hours ago 
 Short answer: You can recover overpaid national taxes from the BIR as a cash refund or a tax credit certificate (TCC). The main claims are excess creditable withholding or income tax (Section 76, NIRC), taxes erroneously or illegally collected (Sections 204(C) and 229), and input VAT on zero-rated sales (Section 112). File a complete application, generally within two years. The BIR has 180 days to decide most claims and 90 days for VAT claims. Missing documents, undeclared income and an earlier carry-over election are common grounds for denial. 
 What tax refunds can you claim from the BIR? 
 The rules are in the Tax Code (NIRC), as amended by the Ease of Paying Taxes (EOPT) Act, Republic Act (RA) No. 11976, effective January 22, 2024, and, for VAT, by RA No. 12066 (CREATE MORE), approved November 8, 2024. There are three main claims: 
 Excess creditable withholding or income tax. A corporation whose income tax paid or withheld during the year exceeds the tax due on its annual return may carry the excess over to the next years or have it refunded or credited (Section 76, NIRC, as amended by RA No. 11976; RMC No. 75-2024). Individuals claim under Section 58(E), which refunds tax withheld in excess of the tax due on the return, subject to Section 204 (RMC No. 14-2025). 
 Taxes erroneously or illegally collected. Tax that was not due, paid twice or paid in excess, and penalties imposed without authority (Sections 204(C) and 229, NIRC, as amended by RA No. 11976). 
 Input VAT on zero-rated or effectively zero-rated sales. Creditable input tax attributable to those sales, to the extent not applied against output tax, except transitional input tax (Section 112(A), NIRC). Unused input tax may also be claimed when a VAT registration is cancelled (Section 112(B), NIRC, as amended by RA No. 11976). 
 Cash or tax credit certificate. You may ask for either. A TCC pays any internal revenue tax you are directly liable for, except withholding taxes, and an unused TCC may be converted into cash, subject to Section 230, if you surrender the original. Incentives under special laws that involved no actual payment are never refunded (Section 204(C), NIRC). A refund check unclaimed or uncashed for five years is forfeited, and a TCC unused five years after issue is invalid unless revalidated (Section 230, NIRC). 
 What are the BIR's current tax refund processing guidelines? 
 Revenue Regulations (RR) No. 5-2024, dated April 11, 2024, implements the EOPT refund rules under Sections 76, 112, 204(C) and 229 for claims filed from July 1, 2024. Separate orders and circulars add the details: 
 Excess creditable withholding tax: Revenue Memorandum Order (RMO) No. 25-2024, as amended by RMO No. 8-2025 (February 19, 2025), on processing; and Revenue Memorandum Circular (RMC) No. 75-2024, as amended by RMC No. 14-2025 (February 19, 2025) and RMC No. 102-2026 (August 3, 2026), on mandatory requirements. 
 Taxes erroneously or illegally collected: RMO No. 27-2024, as amended by RMO No. 25-2026, on processing; and RMC No. 74-2024, as amended by RMC No. 103-2026 (August 5, 2026), on mandatory requirements and where to file. 
 VAT refunds: Section 112(C), NIRC, as amended by RA No. 12066; RR No. 5-2024 on risk-based processing; RR No. 8-2025 on requests for reconsideration; and RMC No. 37-2025, which sets the documentary checklists. 
 What they require: 
 Form. Excess withholding tax and erroneous payment claims are filed on BIR Form No. 1914, Application for Tax Credits/Refunds (RMC No. 102-2026; RMC No. 103-2026). 
 Venue. File with the Revenue District Office (RDO) with jurisdiction over you or, for large taxpayers, the Large Taxpayers Service (LTS) office with jurisdiction. A refund of capital gains tax on real property held as a capital asset, and of the related documentary stamp tax, goes to the RDO where the property is located (RMC No. 102-2026; RMC No. 103-2026). 
 Complete documents only. The BIR receives and processes only applications with every document in its checklist (RMC No. 75-2024; RMC No. 102-2026), and the processing period starts only then (Section 204(C), NIRC). 
 Written reasons. A full or partial denial must state its legal and factual basis (RMO No. 27-2024; Section 112(C), NIRC). 
 How do you file a BIR tax refund claim, step by step? 
 Name the legal basis: Section 76 or 58(E), Sections 204(C) and 229, or Section 112. 
 Check the deadline. It is generally two years: after payment, for erroneous payments (Section 204(C), NIRC); from filing of the annual income tax return, for excess income tax (RR No. 5-2024; RMC No. 102-2026); after the close of the taxable quarter of the zero-rated sales (Section 112(A), NIRC); and from cancellation of a VAT registration (Section 112(B), NIRC). Our guide to the prescriptive period for tax refunds explains how to count each one. 
 Reconcile first. Returns, books, BIR Forms 2307 and invoices should agree. For excess withholding tax claims, returns cannot be amended once the claim is filed or an eLA covers the period, and only returns filed before the application count (RMC No. 14-2025). 
 Assemble the application with the documents listed below, including a notarized taxpayer attestation that they are complete (RMC No. 74-2024; RMC No. 75-2024). 
 File with the proper office, and keep proof of what you filed and when. 
 Cooperate with the verification. Not producing books and records that the revenue officer requests in writing may lead to denial (RMC No. 75-2024). 
 How long does a BIR tax refund take? 
 180 days for erroneous payment claims and regular excess income tax claims, from submission of complete documents (Sections 204(C) and 229, NIRC; RR No. 5-2024). 
 90 days for VAT claims, from submission of certified true copies of invoices and the other prescribed documents (Section 112(C), NIRC, as amended by RA No. 12066). 
 Two years for a corporation that dissolved or ceased business, counted from the dissolution or cessation (Section 76, NIRC, as amended by RA No. 11976). The BIR counts it from submission of BIR Form No. 1905 with complete documents (RMC No. 102-2026), and releases the refund only after a mandatory audit and full settlement of the company's taxes (RR No. 5-2024; RMO No. 25-2024). See closing a business and cancelling your BIR registration . 
 VAT claims are classified as low, medium or high risk, based on factors such as the amount, compliance history and frequency of claims, and medium- and high-risk claims are audited or verified (Section 112(C), NIRC; RR No. 5-2024). 
 What documents do you need to claim a tax refund? 
 Excess creditable withholding tax (corporations): 
 BIR Form 1914, the checklist of mandatory requirements and the notarized taxpayer attestation (RMC No. 75-2024, as amended); 
 the quarterly and annual income tax returns for the year, filed before the application or the eLA, whichever came first (RMC No. 75-2024; RMC No. 14-2025); 
 copies of duly accomplished BIR Forms 2307, or BIR Form 1606 for real property sales, issued by your payors (RMC No. 14-2025), each showing the amount paid and the tax withheld (Section 2.58.3(B), RR No. 2-98); 
 records tracing the income in those certificates to the gross income in your return (Section 58(E), NIRC); and 
 for a business that has closed, BIR Form 1905 with the closure documents (RMC No. 102-2026). 
 Taxes erroneously or illegally collected: 
 BIR Form 1914, the checklist of mandatory requirements and the notarized taxpayer attestation (RMC No. 74-2024); 
 your written claim stating why the tax was not due (Section 204(C), NIRC); 
 a copy of the duly filed return and proof of payment (RR No. 5-2024; RMO No. 27-2024); and 
 the books and records the BIR asks for during verification (RMC No. 74-2024). 
 Input VAT on zero-rated or effectively zero-rated sales: 
 the documents in the BIR checklist for the period covered (RMC No. 37-2025), for which certified true copies of invoices are accepted (Section 112(C), NIRC, as amended by RA No. 12066); 
 VAT returns reporting the zero-rated sales; a claim fails without proof of such sales, and financial statements cannot take the place of VAT returns and official receipts ( Maibarara Geothermal, Inc. v. Commissioner of Internal Revenue , G.R. No. 250479, July 18, 2022); 
 sales invoices with the term "zero-rated sale" written or printed on them (Section 113(B)(2)(c), NIRC, as amended by RA No. 11976); 
 suppliers' VAT invoices supporting each input tax claimed (Section 110(A)(1), NIRC, as amended by RA No. 11976); 
 proof that foreign currency proceeds were accounted for under Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas rules, for the export and service sales listed in Section 112(A); and 
 if you also have taxable or exempt sales, an allocation of common input tax by volume of sales (Section 112(A), NIRC). 
 Can you get a refund after carrying over excess income tax? 
 Generally no. Once a corporation opts to carry the excess over, the option is irrevocable for that taxable period, and no cash refund or TCC is allowed (Section 76, NIRC, as amended by RA No. 11976). 
 The option is made once taken, "actually or constructively," such as by marking the carry-over box on the return, whether or not the credit is ever used. There is no time limit on carrying it over, and choosing one option precludes the other ( Commissioner of Internal Revenue v. Bank of the Philippine Islands , G.R. No. 178490, July 7, 2009). 
 A refund claim is also denied if the same amount is then carried over in the next year's return, though it stays creditable against future income tax (RR No. 5-2024). Where the amount was also applied, the BIR may issue a final assessment without a PAN (Section 228, NIRC; RR No. 12-99, as amended). 
 The one exception: a corporation that cannot use the carry-over because it dissolved or ceased business may apply for a refund (Section 76, NIRC, as amended by RA No. 11976; RMC No. 102-2026). 
 Why does the BIR deny tax refund claims? 
 Lack of substantiation. The taxpayer must prove the claim with sufficient and competent evidence ( Maibarara Geothermal, Inc. v. Commissioner of Internal Revenue , G.R. No. 256720, August 7, 2024). VAT refunds are construed strictly against the taxpayer ( Taihei Alltech Construction (Phil.) Inc. v. Commissioner of Internal Revenue , G.R. No. 258791, December 7, 2022). A claim based on erroneous payment, which the Court applied to excess creditable withholding tax, needs only a preponderance of evidence ( Commissioner of Internal Revenue v. Sonoma Services, Inc. , G.R. No. 263916, August 18, 2025). 
 Unremitted or unreported withholding. Under BIR rules, no income tax refund is granted until the Forms 2307 are verified as authentic, including against the payor's alphalist of payees (RMO No. 25-2024, as amended by RMO No. 8-2025; RMC No. 14-2025). But proof of remittance is the withholding agent's responsibility (Section 2.58.3(B), RR No. 2-98). A claimant's failure to present its Summary Alphalist of Withholding Taxes or the payor's Monthly Alphalist of Payees is not a ground for outright denial, and once the Forms 2307 are presented, the BIR must show they are incomplete, false or irregular ( Sonoma ). See unremitted withholding taxes . 
 Income not declared. The income must be included in the recipient's return (Section 58(E), NIRC). A refund requires showing that it was declared as part of gross income, besides the payor's certificate proving the withholding (Section 2.58.3(B), RR No. 2-98; Sonoma ). 
 Invoicing defects for zero-rated sales. Input tax must be supported by a VAT invoice issued under Section 113 (Section 110(A)(1), NIRC; Commissioner of Internal Revenue v. Toledo Power Company , G.R. Nos. 255324 & 255353, April 12, 2023), and an invoice for a zero-rated sale must show the term "zero-rated sale" (Section 113(B)(2)(c), NIRC, as amended by RA No. 11976). Invoices without the word "zero-rated" defeated an exporter's claim ( Panasonic Communications Imaging Corporation of the Philippines v. Commissioner of Internal Revenue , G.R. No. 178090, February 8, 2010). See BIR e-invoicing rules . 
 Late or premature filing. A claim filed after its two-year period is lost (Sections 112(A) and 204(C), NIRC), and no court case may be filed until the BIR denies the claim or the 180 days lapse (Section 229, NIRC, as amended by RA No. 11976). A VAT denial becomes final unless reconsideration is sought within 15 days (Section 112(C), NIRC, as amended by RA No. 12066). The VAT periods to go to court are mandatory and jurisdictional, and "late filing is absolutely prohibited" ( Taihei Alltech ). 
 Carry-over already elected. See the section above (Section 76, NIRC; Bank of the Philippine Islands ). 
 Does a tax refund claim trigger a BIR audit? 
 Expect at least a verification. An income tax refund or TCC claim brings an electronic Letter of Authority (eLA) covering all internal revenue taxes for that year. A VAT refund claim is verified under a Tax Verification Notice (TVN) limited to that claim, and broader issues need a separate eLA (RMO No. 22-2026; RMC No. 14-2026). The BIR wound up its separate VAT audit units in May 2026, with transition rules for VAT refund applications (RMO No. 6-2026; RMC No. 14-2026). 
 An eLA examination can also end in a deficiency assessment. See what triggers a BIR audit and the BIR tax audit process . 
 What can you do if the BIR denies your refund or does not act? 
 Income tax and erroneous payment claims. Appeal to the Court of Tax Appeals (CTA) within 30 days from receipt of a full or partial denial. If the BIR does not decide within 180 days, you may appeal within 30 days after the 180 days end, or wait for the decision. If you appeal, the administrative claim becomes moot (Section 229, NIRC, as amended by RA No. 11976; RR No. 5-2024; RMO No. 25-2024; RMO No. 27-2024). 
 VAT claims. Ask for reconsideration within 15 days from receipt of the denial, or the decision becomes final. The Commissioner has 15 days to decide it. You may then appeal to the CTA within 30 days from receipt of the denial of reconsideration, or from the end of the 90-day or 15-day period if the BIR does not act (Section 112(C), NIRC, as amended by RA No. 12066; RR No. 8-2025). 
 For counting these periods, see refund deadlines and CTA appeals ; for the petition and the evidence, see how to appeal a BIR decision to the CTA and burden of proof at the CTA . 
 Frequently asked questions 
 Is the overpayment shown in my income tax return enough to claim a refund? 
 A return showing an overpayment counts as a written claim (Section 204(C), NIRC). But the BIR processes the claim only if you also file BIR Form 1914 and complete documents within the two years (RMC No. 102-2026). 
 Do I have to pay under protest to claim a refund? 
 No. A refund case may be pursued whether or not the tax was paid under protest or duress (Section 229, NIRC). 
 Can the BIR refund a tax without a written claim? 
 Yes, where the return shows on its face that the payment was clearly erroneous (Section 229, NIRC, as amended by RA No. 11976). 
 How long is a tax credit certificate valid? 
 Five years from issue, unless revalidated. After that, it cannot be used to pay taxes and the amount reverts to the general fund (Section 230, NIRC). 
 Can individuals claim a refund of excess creditable withholding tax? 
 Yes, under Section 58(E) in relation to Section 204, NIRC. The BIR has said it will prescribe separate mandatory requirements for individual claimants (RMC No. 14-2025).
